New BMW Alpina 7 Series Takes Shape in Fantasy Land, Packs a Punchy V8 Motor
6 photos
Photo: Kolesa
Do you remember the new BMW Alpina 7 Series that we first encountered at the end of last month (October 2026)? Why, of course you do, because such a thing is not easily forgotten.
Subsequent to it being scooped in the open, it was sent to the Nardo racetrack in Italy for more testing, where it managed to reach 186 mph (300 kph). Keep in mind that it wasn’t built for speed but comfort, yet it certainly features a big dose of sportiness. After all, it’s an Alpina, and for decades, these models have been able to mix the sporty driving credentials with the comfort-oriented ones perfectly, while adding a big dose of novelties both inside and out.
Therefore, the upcoming BMW Alpina 7 Series will continue to do so, just like the previous-generation B7, and if you are wondering why it won’t be christened the Alpina B7, it is because the company is now part of the BMW Group. As for the family that founded Alpina, it is back in business under the Bovensiepen name . And they have quite a couple new products in their lineup, which follow a similar theme, including the 05 GT, based on the BMW M5 Touring, and the Spider, building on the Z4.
Now, while BMW Alpina is fine-tuning the new 7 Series in different environments, the pixel-altering crowd has started removing the camouflage on the car’s body using photo-editing software. One of the first rendering takes on this model that has crossed our screens came from Kolesa. The CGI’s shared in the gallery were the work of Nikita Chuyko, and they are very realistic, as they were based on the actual scoops mentioned above, and the car is sprinkled with the usual Alpina goodies.
Photo: Kolesa Compared to the latest BMW 7 Series , the Alpina variant features a new bumper at the front with redesigned vents on the sides and a new air intake in the middle that is narrower but taller. The integrated splitter is another novelty, and so are the yellow daytime running lights that will probably not be a thing. And if they are, then we have yet to see them on a prototype. Spy shots have revealed that the grille should feature a different pattern, though for what it’s worth, it carries over from the regular 7er on this CGI model.
The changes continue at the rear, where the vehicle sports a new bumper with vertical instead of horizontal reflectors that now sit further up. The diffuser is also more aggressive than the one equipping the regular BMW 7 Series, and has cutouts for four exhaust tips. A pair of pinstripe-like lines decorate the car’s profile, stretching from the front fenders to the taillights, and displaying Alpina’s name on them.
This rendered BMW Alpina 7 Series has a green paint finish on the outside, typical of other Alpina models, and rides on the sought-after wheels with their V-spoke pattern, which are much larger than the ones equipping the standard 7er. The imagined car also has a slightly lower ground clearance for faster cornering, and it displays its name in the middle of the splitter, and on the left-hand side of the trunk lid.
Photo: Kolesa Its interior has yet to open up to the camera, but expect the same Panoramic iDrive, free-floating infotainment system, and passenger display as the latest BMW 7 Series. However, we believe that new submenus and load screens will be part of the Alpina makeover alongside a new steering wheel, and different trim and upholstery, as well as perhaps exclusive treadplates, among other things.
BMW has already confirmed that the upcoming Alpina 7 Series will feature a V8 engine, and it is likely the unit powering the new M760 xDrive. The automaker hasn’t revealed the full specs, but it did confirm that the mill, which is a twin-turbo 4.4-liter V8, will produce approximately 570 hp, which is a bit more than the old 760i that had 563 hp on tap. If anything, the lump should produce more oomph in the new Alpina, and over 600 horsepower seems very likely, this writer believes.
The BMW Alpina 7 Series will sit at the very top of the latest 7er lineup, and it is expected to arrive in the United States of America for the 2028 model year. Thus, there may not be an M7, but the Alpina will definitely fill this void, combining plenty of oomph, sporty driving credentials, exclusive looks, and a comfortable ride like a real champ.
By the way, the 7er won’t be the only modern Bimmer that will get the Alpina treatment, as so will the next-generation X7 that is now in the making. But what’s your take on the design of the BMW Alpina 7 Series, as it was imagined by the quoted rendering artist? Do you fancy the look?
